title: The mole at a glance
lines: | gas volume at STP | V ÷ 22.4 dm³
- Empirical formula: divide by atomic mass, then by the smallest result.
- Limiting reactant: smallest value of moles ÷ coefficient.
! Molecules or atoms? 9 g of water is 0.5 mol: 3.01 × 10²³ molecules but 9.03 × 10²³ atoms.

title: Gas laws
lines: | Dalton | P(total) = p₁ + p₂ + … | V, T
- PV = nRT; R = 0.0821 dm³ atm K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹.
- Real gases are most ideal at low pressure and high temperature.
! H₂ diffuses 4 times as fast as O₂ (√(32/2) = 4).

title: Intermolecular forces and solids
lines: - Strength for similar sizes: London < dipole-dipole < hydrogen bond.
- Hydrogen bonds need H on F, O or N: water boils at 100 °C, H₂S is a gas.
- Boiling point: vapour pressure = external pressure.
| Ionic | NaCl | only molten or dissolved
| Covalent network | diamond, SiO₂ | no (graphite yes)
| Metallic | Cu | yes, as a solid
! Ice is less dense than water because hydrogen bonds hold its molecules in an open lattice.

title: Atomic particles and quantum numbers
lines: | Particle | Relative mass | Charge | Found through
- n shell; l = 0 to n − 1 (s, p, d, f); m = −l to +l; s = ±½.
- Shell holds 2n²; subshells s 2, p 6, d 10, f 14.

title: Filling orbitals
lines: - Pauli: at most 2 electrons per orbital, opposite spins.
- Hund: fill degenerate orbitals singly, spins parallel, before pairing.
! N (2p³) has 3 unpaired electrons, O (2p⁴) has 2.

title: VSEPR shapes
lines: | Bond pairs, lone pairs | Shape | Angle | Example
! Repulsion: lone-lone > lone-bond > bond-bond, so CH₄ > NH₃ > H₂O in bond angle.

title: Hybridisation and bond order
lines: - Single = σ; double = σ + π; triple = σ + 2π. Ethene 5σ 1π; ethyne 3σ 2π.
- Bond order = (bonding − antibonding electrons) ÷ 2: N₂ 3, O₂ 2, He₂ 0.
- O₂ is paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons), explained only by MO theory.
! Symmetrical CO₂, BF₃ and CCl₄ have zero dipole moment despite polar bonds.

title: Thermochemistry
lines: - Exothermic ΔH < 0; endothermic ΔH > 0. Standard: 298 K, 1 atm.
| formation | zero for an element in its standard state
| neutralisation | about −57 kJ/mol (strong acid + strong base)
- Hess: ΔH is the same by any route; ΔH = ΣΔH(f, products) − ΣΔH(f, reactants).
- Reverse an equation: change the sign of ΔH.
- ΔG = ΔH − TΔS; spontaneous when ΔG < 0.

title: Equilibrium and Le Chatelier
lines: - Kc = [products]^coefficients ÷ [reactants]^coefficients; leave out pure solids and liquids.
- Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn (Δn = change in gas moles).
| raise pressure | to fewer gas moles | no
- Q < K: goes forward; Q > K: goes backward.

title: Acids, bases and pH
lines: | Arrhenius | gives H⁺ in water | gives OH⁻ in water
- NH₄Cl solution is acidic; CH₃COONa is basic; NaCl is neutral.
- Indicators: methyl orange for strong acid + weak base; phenolphthalein for weak acid + strong base.
! Diluting a strong acid tenfold raises pH by 1, but never above 7.

title: Reaction kinetics
lines: - Rate = k[A]ˣ[B]ʸ; order = x + y, found by experiment.
- Arrhenius k = Ae^(−Ea/RT); a 10 K rise roughly doubles the rate near room temperature.
! A catalyst lowers Ea for both directions; ΔH and K do not change.

title: Oxidation numbers: OIL RIG
lines: Mnemonic "OIL RIG": Oxidation Is Loss of electrons, Reduction Is Gain.
- Elements 0; F always −1; sum = charge on the species.
- Mn +7 in KMnO₄; Cr +6 in K₂Cr₂O₇; S +6 in H₂SO₄.
- The oxidising agent is reduced; the reducing agent is oxidised.
! Disproportionation: Cl₂ + cold NaOH gives Cl⁻ (−1) and OCl⁻ (+1).

title: Cells and electrolysis
lines: | Energy | chemical to electrical | electrical to chemical
- E°(cell) = E°(cathode) − E°(anode); Daniell cell 1.10 V.
- 1 F = 96,500 C per mole of electrons.
- 1 F deposits 108 g Ag, 31.75 g Cu, 9 g Al, or 11.2 dm³ H₂ at STP.
! Metals with more negative E° are stronger reducing agents and displace H₂ from acids.

title: Solutions and colligative properties
lines: - Molarity: mol per dm³ of solution. Molality: mol per kg of solvent.
- Mole fraction: moles of component ÷ total moles.
- Raoult: vapour pressure ∝ mole fraction of the solvent.
- ΔT(b) = Kb m (water 0.52); ΔT(f) = Kf m (water 1.86 K kg mol⁻¹).
- Electrolytes: multiply by particles per formula (NaCl 2, CaCl₂ 3).
! Molality does not change with temperature; molarity does.

title: Periodic trends
lines: | Property | Across a period | Down a group
- IE exceptions: Be > B, Mg > Al; N > O, P > S.
- Isoelectronic: O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > Al³⁺.
- Period 3 oxides: basic (Na, Mg), amphoteric (Al), acidic (Si to Cl).
! Electronegativity: F > O > N ≈ Cl > C > H.

title: Groups 1 and 2
lines: - Group 2 down: hydroxides more soluble, sulphates less soluble (BaSO₄ insoluble).
- Diagonal pairs: Li with Mg, Be with Al.
! Plaster of Paris CaSO₄·½H₂O; gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O.

title: Halogens and noble gases
lines: | Halogen | State at room temperature | AgX precipitate
| F₂ | pale yellow gas | none (AgF soluble)
- Oxidising power F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂.
- Acid strength HI > HBr > HCl > HF.
- Xenon forms XeF₂ (linear), XeF₄ (square planar), XeF₆.
! The strongest X–X bond is Cl–Cl, not F–F.

title: Transition elements
lines: - Variable oxidation states, coloured ions, paramagnetism, complexes, catalysis.
- MnO₄⁻ (purple) → Mn²⁺ gains 5 e⁻; Cr₂O₇²⁻ (orange) → Cr³⁺ (green) gains 6 e⁻.

title: Industrial processes
lines: | Ostwald | HNO₃ | Pt-Rh gauze | NH₃ oxidised to NO
| Solvay | Na₂CO₃ | none | NaCl, NH₃, CO₂, limestone
| Hydrogenation | vanaspati ghee | nickel | oil + H₂
- Urea CO(NH₂)₂: 46.7 % N; ammonium nitrate 35 %; ammonium sulphate 21.2 %.
! SO₃ is absorbed in 98 % H₂SO₄ (oleum), not in water.

title: Functional groups and names
lines: - Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, alkenes CₙH₂ₙ, alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
! Isomer counts: C₄H₁₀ 2, C₅H₁₂ 3, C₄H₁₀O 4 alcohols + 3 ethers.

title: Organic reaction types
lines: - Markovnikov: H adds to the carbon with more H.
- Aqueous KOH substitutes; alcoholic KOH eliminates.

title: Tests for organic compounds
lines: | Bromine water | C=C, phenol | decolourised (white ppt with phenol)
| Baeyer's (cold KMnO₄) | C=C | purple colour lost
| Iodoform | CH₃CO– or CH₃CH(OH)– | yellow precipitate
! Lucas test: 3° alcohol cloudy at once, 2° in minutes, 1° not at room temperature.

title: Polymers
lines: ! Condensation polymers lose water at each link; addition polymers lose nothing.

title: Biomolecules
lines: - Glucose: aldohexose; fructose: ketohexose; both C₆H₁₂O₆.
- Sucrose = glucose + fructose, non-reducing; maltose and lactose reduce Fehling's.
- Starch and cellulose: polymers of glucose.
- Proteins: amino acids joined by peptide bonds –CO–NH–; n amino acids, n − 1 bonds.
- Fats: triglycerides; alkaline hydrolysis is saponification (soap).
- DNA: A–T and G–C pairs; RNA uses uracil instead of thymine.
- Enzymes are proteins; heat denatures them.
! Glycine is the only common amino acid without a chiral carbon.
